structure.title: A public investigation
structure.text: Oedipus seeks the cause of Thebes' suffering through testimony, accusation, and attempts to establish an earlier crime.

structure.title: Knowledge under pressure
structure.text: New accounts change the meaning of earlier statements. The chorus registers the city's hopes and fears as the inquiry tightens.

people.name: Oedipus
people.text: The ruler of Thebes, famous for solving the Sphinx's riddle, who vows to find the cause of the plague on his city and will not stop asking.

people.name: Jocasta
people.text: Oedipus's wife, who tries to calm the quarrels in the palace and urges him not to put too much faith in prophecies.

people.name: Tiresias
people.text: The blind prophet Oedipus sends for, who knows the answer to his question and begs to be allowed to go home without giving it.

context.title: A wounded city
context.text: The plague makes the inquiry a public duty. Oedipus' wish to uncover truth begins as a commitment to people seeking his help.
context.takeaway: Intelligence and responsibility drive the investigation.

context.title: The chorus
context.text: The chorus speaks as a collective observer within the drama. Its uncertainty and revisions should not automatically be treated as the author's verdict.
context.takeaway: Hear a community trying to understand.

notice.text: Track changes in who possesses information.
notice.why: Power and knowledge do not remain in the same hands.
Physical sight and understanding repeatedly diverge.

opening: Thebes is dying of plague, and Oedipus intends to save it. He has solved a deadly riddle before; now he must find the murderer whose unpunished crime is poisoning the city. Witnesses resist, warnings accumulate, and the king grows furious at anyone withholding information. Sophocles makes the investigation terrifying because Oedipus' determination is so understandable. He takes responsibility, demands evidence, and refuses convenient silence, bringing the full force of his intelligence to a discovery that others would prefer him never to make.
